_note: Two layers. (1) Index: each stage lists the broad syllabus area(s) it sits in (covers_syllabus_refs / syllabus_topic, as the source spec names them). (2) Coverage: _syllabus_items is the specification broken into its own atomic items, and each stage lists the item ids it teaches in covers_items, so coverage_check.py can say whether the WHOLE specification is taught. Top-level keys starting with _ are metadata, never stages.

_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the areas a stage is principally associated with; it does not claim exhaustive coverage of those areas, exam weighting, or official stage boundaries. Coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms (declared coverage, not verified teaching).

_items_source.document: AQA GCSE English Language 8700 specification: sections 2 (Specification at a glance), 3.1 (Scope of study: 3.1.1 Critical reading and comprehension, 3.1.2 Writing, 3.1.3 Spoken language), 4.1-4.6 (Scheme of assessment, assessment objectives AO1-AO9, weightings) and 5 (Non-exam assessment administration); plus the question types of Papers 1 and 2 from the published question papers and mark schemes
_items_source.version: Version 1.6, March 2026 (numbering follows the spec's own section numbers; the spec's bulleted requirements in 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 are unnumbered, so their clauses are numbered 3.1.1.1, 3.1.1.2 ... in order of appearance; question items use the paper and question number, e.g. P1.Q2; grammar/terminology and technique items T., W., X. are course-defined and listed under the spec's requirement for grammatical terminology and linguistic conventions)
